cards.title: The Path Between Us
cards.description: Two simplified people stand side by side, seen from behind at a slightly elevated angle. Their inward-facing silhouettes leave a tapered Paper-white opening that reads as a path continuing into the distance. Neither is pulling, rescuing or leading the other. Both face the same open space.
cards.meaning: the relationship makes room for possibility.
cards.colour: deep teal and coral figures; a tiny peach sun ahead; white pathway.
cards.note: the gap must deliberately read as a route. Keep it broad and avoid complicated arms. The young person should not look like a tiny child next to a giant adult.

cards.title: Different Shoes, Shared Direction
cards.description: An overhead view of two pairs of shoes pointing toward the same opening in a curved pavement edge. One pair is expressive and youthful; the other quieter. Both have similar visual weight. Their long shadows overlap into one calm shape.
cards.meaning: being alongside someone, expressed through an ordinary moment.
cards.colour: coral trainers, deep teal shoes, a small sage ground fragment and apricot shadow.
cards.note: show just enough of the legs to establish the viewpoint. Avoid a busy street scene. The shadows are the only secondary idea.

cards.title: Space To Unfold
cards.description: A folded coral paper form opens into a broad peach surface. A small figure stands comfortably at the fold, with generous room ahead. The folds suggest developing possibilities rather than a staircase to success.
cards.meaning: growth can reveal space that was already there.
cards.colour: coral, peach and deep plum on Paper.
cards.note: three or four folds maximum. It should still read as paper, not an impossible architectural puzzle.

cards.title: The Book That Becomes A Bridge
cards.description: An open book viewed low enough that its lifted page blocks form a gentle arch. The same object reads as both an open book and a short bridge. cards.colour: deep teal cover, apricot pages, coral figure.
cards.note: an approachable little crossing, not a dangerous bridge over a canyon. No extra landscape or flying pages.

cards.title: The Gap Makes Sense

cards.colour: plum and coral stacks with a pale apricot page edge.
cards.note: this is a harder generation challenge. Begin with two flat silhouettes and simplify until the hidden key reads. Avoid suggesting that one tool solves everything.

cards.title: The Home Between The Branches
cards.description: Two broad organic branches lean toward one another. Their inner contours leave a small house-shaped opening in Paper white: sloping roof, upright sides and flat base. Five simple leaves sit around the outside. The house is never drawn or outlined; it exists only as the gap.
cards.meaning: family and belonging are held within the living structure.
cards.colour: evergreen branches, sage leaves and one coral accent.
cards.note: do not add windows, a door or a second house on top. The house is an emotional metaphor for belonging, not a claim about a particular home.

cards.colour: sage, coral, peach, teal and plum, with a mostly Paper-white cup.
cards.note: keep the handle believable. Five is a quiet family reference. Do not assign colours to ethnic backgrounds or invent a cultural weaving pattern.

cards.note: broad graceful channels, not a dense botanical diagram. This is the simpler alternative if the hidden house in concept 9 proves difficult to generate.

cards.note: one transformed shadow only. No extra arrows, graph, book or lighthouse. Keep other lighting cues minimal so the intentional shadow makes sense.

Avoid photorealism, 3D rendering, glossy surfaces, grain, sketchy hatching, busy scenery and hairline-only artwork. Do not add a logo, letters, captions, watermarks or readable text. Do not invent cultural motifs or ornamental patterns.

COMPOSITION AND OUTPUT: One isolated illustration in a landscape 13:10 canvas, ideally 1560 x 1200 px. Keep the complete subject within the canvas, with at least 10% breathing room on every side. Place its visual centre slightly below the canvas centre, leaving generous empty space above. Background must be transparent; if transparency is unavailable, use pure Paper white #FFFFFF with no coloured rectangle or vignette. No frame or border. Keep shadows minimal and contained within the object. Produce only the illustration, not a webpage mockup. Use the palette specified below selectively, rather than putting every brand colour into the image.

SUBJECT: A highly simplified lighthouse made from four or five carefully balanced filled shapes: a soft tapered tower, small lantern, shallow roof, tiny arched doorway and a restrained curved base. The tower is slightly off-centre left, leaving generous space for one warm beam to the right. Add only two short curved water marks at the base. Give the silhouette gentle asymmetry and soften sharp corners without making it toy-like. This is the most minimal option in the set.

COLOUR: Paper white #FFFFFF tower defined by a deep teal #02364A side plane, deep plum #281A2C roof and small doorway, sage #A4B57A base accent, warm peach #FDB069 lantern and pale apricot #FDD8B1 beam. Ink #191919 may be used for a tiny structural accent, not a heavy outline around everything.

MEANING: Quiet clarity and a useful next step. Give it the same warmth and calm visual confidence as the community illustration, with far fewer shapes. Avoid a generic app icon, enclosing badge, hard black contour, glossy finish, lettering or extra scenery.
